description.short: One of China's earliest black teas exported to Europe, featuring a sweet honeyed-fruit profile
description.overview: Historically one of China's premier 19th-century export black teas, which alongside Keemun shaped the Western conception of Chinese black tea.
description.taste: Mellow and gently sweet with fruity notes
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Black tea production in the region (historically known as Ningzhou, which gave the tea its name) began in the 19th century in response to surging demand from European traders
history.development: At the peak of its popularity in the late 19th century, Ninghong was celebrated as one of China's foremost export black teas alongside Keemun
history.modern: Today less widely recognized outside China than during the height of the tea trade, but maintains its status as a historically significant regional black tea
interestingFacts: In the 19th century, Ning Hong and Keemun were direct rivals in the European export trade, each competing for the reputation of China's finest black tea
The historic name 'Ningzhou' is largely absent from modern administrative divisions, but remains preserved in the tea's name
